- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the following 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean price in early periods; apply a “mean reversion bias” — subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if recent 7-day average is higher than 30-day average.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses the direction; align forecast with sentiment direction — if sentiment >0.5, forecast should be slightly higher; if <0.5, slightly lower.
